capstone-record: Two-panel chart for Fish River near Fort Kent, ME, 1 October 1995 to 30 September 2000. Top: observed daily discharge in cubic metres per second with one sharp spring peak each year, up to about 306 in April 1996; days above the P95 threshold of 170.9 are shaded amber with diagonal hatching and occur in the spring peaks of 1996, 1997, 1998, 1999 and 2000. Bottom: mean discharge by calendar month, highest in April and May and lowest in the late summer.
capstone-signatures: Flow duration curve for Fish River: discharge on a logarithmic axis from about 1 to 300 cubic metres per second against exceedance probability from 0 to 100 percent. The curve falls smoothly from about 300 at the left to about 10 at 90 percent and drops steeply to about 1 at the far right. Title: Lyne-Hollick BFI 0.557.
capstone-twi: Two panels for a SYNTHETIC 24 by 24 hillslope. Left: a map of the topographic wetness index in a purple-to-yellow scale, mostly low values (6 to 8) with a brighter meandering valley line of high values (10 to 16) running down the centre to the outlet at the bottom. Right: histogram of TWI values with most cells between 6 and 9; dashed line at the mean of 7.62 and dotted line at the upper tercile of 7.98.
